displayDescription: One cream disc splits into teal and orange halves, which send out nodes that build a connected lattice on a dark slate field.
styleRenderer: SVG (inline, hand-authored shape groups with shared coordinates)
d3-interpolate 3.0.1 interpolateString (path morphing, bundled locally with esbuild to d3-interpolate.bundle.js)
motionEngine: GSAP 3 paused timeline at window.__timelines.video (transforms, opacity, stroke dash draws)
Time-derived draw(t) function, called from the timeline render and hf-seek, which owns morph path d, echo bands, node travel and HUD readouts
limitations: Blender was not used, per the user's instruction. The scene is flat 2D SVG vector work, which suits this flat-geometry style. There is no 3D depth or lighting.
Path morphing uses d3-interpolate's string interpolation between half-disc paths that share the same command structure. It is not a general shape-matching morph.
The stepped echo bands are lagging outline copies standing in for motion blur. This follows the reference craft and is not physical blur.
The HUD timecode, chapter counter and resolution readout are design elements, not real measured data.
The background (#1B2C33 to #0E171C vignette) was picked for this scene following the source-frame review. The earlier #F6F0E2 swatch now serves as the light ink role.

STYLE.json has no tech.preview_recipes. This refresh shows the reviewed source-frame techniques instead: a quiet low-chroma field, light line ink, one reserved hot accent, a HUD frame and stepped echoes.
Rendering and browser QA were not run by the agent. The host runs them.
